parakeet: We don't currently have those conditions at scale. So defense first strategies exhaust people without dislodging the system. You don't defeat supremacist ideology by opposing it directly. You defeat it by interrupting the conditions that allow it to reproduce. Christian nationalism survives because it keeps people economically fragile, socially isolated, psychologically dependent, and existentially insecure. Supremacy doesn't need mass agreement. It needs mass vulnerability. To make it plain, supremacist theism functions like legacy software. It's installed early, rarely audited, reinforced socially, and updated emotionally, not logically. You can't argue someone out of software, they're still running. You have to reduce the dependency, increase the agency, and then create alternative environments where different patterns can form. That requires time, trust, and repetition, not confrontation. Now I have to make this clear and answer the question why we're not ready for defensive posture yet. Now, this is an important and honest admission. Defense requires psychological resilience, economic margin, social backing, and coordinated infrastructure. Most people emerging from supremacist systems lack all four. So calls to fight, resist, or stand up are premature and often re-traumatizing. You don't send people into battle before they've eaten, slept, healed, or trained.
